package_info.why_malicious: All versions of Jinja2 prior to 3.1.3 are vulnerable to a cross-site scripting (XSS) flaw (CVE-2024-22195) in the xmlattr filter, which allows attackers to inject arbitrary HTML attributes and potentially execute untrusted scripts in users' browsers. This vulnerability can be exploited if user-controlled input is passed to the xmlattr filter, bypassing the intended auto-escaping mechanism.

execution_context.file_location: Python application code using Jinja2 templates (e.g., j2_xmlattr.py, or any template rendering context)
required_permissions: network (if template output is served over HTTP)
environment_vars (if user input is passed from environment)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
tmpl = Template(u'''\
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <title>{{ title|escape }}</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    <img{{ dict_var|xmlattr }}>
  </body>
</html>
''')
...
data = {
    key: 'xxx',
    'src': 'https://jinja.palletsprojects.com/en/3.0.x/_static/jinja-logo-sidebar.png',
    'alt': 'My image'
}
print(tmpl.render(
    title='Jinja2 xmlattr PoC',
    dict_var=data
))
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code renders a Jinja2 template that uses the xmlattr filter on a dictionary containing user-controlled keys, allowing arbitrary HTML attributes to be injected into an tag, which can result in XSS if malicious attributes (e.g., onerror) are supplied.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code allows user input to directly control HTML attribute names and values in a rendered template, bypassing the intended auto-escaping and enabling XSS payload injection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, template engines like Jinja2 are expected to prevent XSS by escaping user input and not allowing arbitrary attribute injection. Here, the xmlattr filter fails to sanitize keys with spaces or special characters, violating this expectation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of xmlattr is to dynamically set safe, validated HTML attributes from trusted sources. However, user input should always be sanitized or validated before being used as attribute names or values.
key_indicators: Use of xmlattr filter with user-controlled dictionary keys
No sanitization or validation of attribute names
Ability to inject attributes like onerror or src via user input

attack_chain.action: User input is accepted as a key for an HTML attribute in a dictionary passed to the template.
attack_chain.leads_to: User input is used unsafely in template rendering.

attack_chain.action: Jinja2 template renders an tag with attributes generated from the user-controlled dictionary using the xmlattr filter.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary HTML attributes are injected into the output.

attack_chain.action: If a malicious attribute (e.g., onerror) is injected, the browser executes attacker-supplied JavaScript when the image fails to load or another event occurs.
attack_chain.leads_to: Cross-site scripting (XSS) is achieved, allowing attacker code execution in the user's browser.

behavioral_signatures: Use of xmlattr filter in Jinja2 templates with user-controlled dictionary keys
Rendering templates where attribute names are not statically defined
Presence of keys with spaces or special characters in attribute dictionaries
file_indicators: Python code passing unsanitized user input as dictionary keys to template rendering
network_indicators: Unusual outbound requests from browsers to attacker-controlled domains after visiting a site using vulnerable templates (indicative of XSS exploitation)
HTTP responses containing or other tags with suspicious attributes (e.g., onerror, onclick) not present in source code
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan Jinja2 templates for use of the xmlattr filter with non-static or user-controlled dictionaries. Audit Python code for instances where user input is used as dictionary keys passed to template rendering. Check requirements.txt or pip freeze output for Jinja2 versions below 3.1.3. Monitor web application responses for injected HTML attributes or evidence of XSS payloads. Use static analysis tools to flag dynamic attribute injection patterns.
